A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 27-page versions of iMontage. Their complete main texts, tables, equations, figures, and supplementary material support comparison, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, storyboard-generation results, a 50-participant user study, and RoPE and training-schedule ablations in Sections 4 and 8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including Tables 1–4 and the supplementary evaluations and qualitative results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same HunyuanVideo-based architecture, Marginal RoPE, prompt interface, flow-matching objective, and three-stage training scheme. No algorithmic or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: The training corpora and multitask subsets are unchanged. Both evaluate GEdit-GPT4o-EN, ImgEdit, OmniContext, and storyboard generation, alongside the same qualitative editing, reference-conditioning, style-transfer, and multi-view scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical comparator membership, including StoryDiffusion, UNO with UMO, and OmniGen2 with UMO for storyboard evaluation. Frame2Frame is newly cited in related work but is not added to any evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Training settings in Table 5, benchmark metrics, inference settings, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both retain the 20-example, 50-participant user study and the same model-specific resolutions, guidance scales, and inference steps.

E4.justification: Both contain the same Marginal versus Even RoPE ablation, FlatMix/StageMix/CocktailMix analyses, and failure cases. Sections 4.4, 8.3, and 9.2 and Figures 5 and 11 provide unchanged analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Section 8.2 retains the same random-seed description, rating aggregation, and controls for participant variability. Neither version adds repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 match, including iMontage's ImgEdit average of 4.11 and OmniContext average of 7.41. The reported 12.6% CocktailMix advantage and all qualitative result images also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The identity-preservation and temporal-consistency definitions in Section 8.1, Equations (1)–(2), are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified many-to-many generation, dynamic outputs, temporal/content consistency, and competitive performance. The contribution list and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations of the ablations are unchanged. Both retain the best-quality qualification of up to four inputs and outputs and the same Chinese-text, background-leakage, and facial-detail limitations and proposed remedies.

D1.justification: Section 6, Table 5, and the supplementary evaluation instructions retain identical implementation and reproducibility information. The homepage's displayed label changes, but its hyperlink destination is identical; the promise to release code and weights is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Frame2Frame alongside RealGeneral as another video-backbone approach, with a new reference to Rotstein et al., Pathways on the Image Manifold: Image Editing via Video Generation. Other references are retained and renumbered; the broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Haoling Xie to the byline and a funding acknowledgement before the references, updates the project-leader symbol and homepage label, and makes a small Figure 11 caption correction. The narrative and section organization are otherwise preserved.

P2.justification: All 19 figures and five tables retain their imagery and display structures. v3 removes printed page numbers and introduces limited title-block, text-flow, bibliography-layout, and caption changes, without redesigning the scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves attribution and contextual completeness by acknowledging the directly relevant Frame2Frame predecessor in Section 2.2 and disclosing funding support. The methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited.
